plan.title: Explore dataset structure and statistics
plan.description: Write scratch.py to load annotations.json and metadata.json. Print: number of images, annotations, categories, annotations per image distribution, category frequency distribution, image sizes, number of products with reference images, bbox size distribution. Also check what's in data/train/ (images subfolder?) and data/products/ structure.
plan.success_criteria: Clear understanding of data properties: image sizes, class distribution, annotation density, reference image availability, and file structure documented in output.

plan.title: Understand train/val split and COCO format compatibility
plan.description: Write scratch.py to: (1) Check if ultralytics can directly consume COCO format or if conversion to YOLO format is needed. (2) Create a train/val split (e.g., 80/20 stratified by store section if identifiable, or random). (3) Verify bbox format and visualize a few annotated images to confirm correctness. (4) Check which category_ids actually appear in annotations vs the 357 defined categories.
plan.success_criteria: Working train/val split created. Visualization confirms bbox annotations are correct. Understanding of format conversion needs.

plan.title: Detection-only baseline with YOLOv8 (all classes mapped to single class)
plan.hypothesis: A YOLOv8m model trained for detection-only (single class) on 248 images can achieve detection_mAP@0.5 > 0.5, giving final_score > 0.35
plan.description: Convert annotations to YOLO format with all category_id=0 (single class detection). Train YOLOv8m with default settings on the train split. Evaluate on val split. Generate submission with all predictions having category_id=0. This establishes the detection ceiling (max 0.7 final score).

plan.title: Optimize detection-only YOLOv8 with better hyperparameters
plan.hypothesis: Tuning image size (1280+), augmentation, and training epochs will improve detection mAP by 5-10%
plan.description: Train YOLOv8m/l with: larger input size (1280), more epochs (100+), appropriate augmentation for dense shelf detection (mosaic, mixup adjustments). Experiment with confidence threshold and NMS IoU threshold tuning for dense predictions. Try YOLOv8l if memory allows.

plan.title: Multi-class YOLOv8 baseline (full 357 categories)
plan.hypothesis: Training YOLOv8 with all 357 categories will give lower detection mAP but add classification score, potentially improving final_score
plan.description: Convert annotations to YOLO format with all 357 category IDs. Train YOLOv8m/l with all classes. Compare detection_mAP and classification_mAP against detection-only baseline. Compute final_score = 0.7*det + 0.3*cls.

plan.title: Two-stage approach: detect then classify with crop-based classifier
plan.hypothesis: Using detection-only model for proposals + separate classifier on crops will outperform end-to-end multi-class detection
plan.description: Stage 1: Use best detection-only model to get bounding boxes. Stage 2: Crop each detected box from the image, resize to 224x224, classify using a ResNet/EfficientNet trained on cropped annotations. Train classifier on all annotated crops from training set. Evaluate the two-stage pipeline.

plan.title: Leverage product reference images for classification via feature matching
plan.hypothesis: Using DINOv2/CLIP features from reference product images as a gallery, and matching detected crops against this gallery, will improve classification accuracy especially for rare classes
plan.description: Extract features from all product reference images using a pretrained vision model (timm DINOv2 or similar). For each detected crop, extract features and find nearest neighbor in the reference gallery. Use product_code to map back to category_id. Compare against trained classifier approach.
plan.success_criteria: Classification accuracy on crops > trained classifier, especially for rare categories

plan.title: Larger YOLOv8 model and SAHI/tiled inference for dense detection
plan.hypothesis: Using tiled/sliding window inference on high-res images will catch small products missed by standard inference
plan.description: Implement SAHI-style tiled inference: split each image into overlapping tiles, run detection on each tile, merge with WBF (Weighted Boxes Fusion from ensemble-boxes). Compare against single-pass inference. Also try YOLOv8x if it fits in memory.
plan.success_criteria: detection_mAP@0.5 improvement of 3%+ over single-pass inference

plan.title: Train classifier with reference image augmentation
plan.hypothesis: Adding product reference images (with augmentation to simulate shelf appearance) to classifier training data will improve classification, especially for rare classes
plan.description: For each product with reference images, apply augmentations (color jitter, perspective transform, crop, blur) to simulate how they look on shelves. Add these to the classifier training set alongside real crops. Train and evaluate.
plan.success_criteria: Classification mAP improvement over crop-only classifier

plan.title: Ensemble detection models with WBF
plan.hypothesis: Ensembling multiple detection models (different sizes, different training configs) with Weighted Boxes Fusion will improve detection mAP
plan.description: Train 2-3 YOLOv8 variants (m, l, x or different augmentation configs). At inference, run all models and merge predictions using WBF from ensemble-boxes package. Tune WBF parameters (iou_threshold, skip_box_thr, weights).

plan.title: Hybrid classification: combine trained classifier + reference matching
plan.hypothesis: Combining classifier logits with reference image similarity scores will be more robust than either alone
plan.description: For each detected crop, get: (1) classifier softmax probabilities, (2) reference image similarity scores. Combine them (weighted average, or use reference matching for rare classes and classifier for common ones). Tune combination weights on validation set.
plan.success_criteria: final_score improvement over either method alone

plan.title: Optimize inference pipeline for 300s sandbox constraint
plan.hypothesis: The full pipeline (detection + classification) can run within 300 seconds on L4 GPU
plan.description: Profile the inference pipeline. Optimize: batch processing for classifier, ONNX export for detection model if needed, efficient image loading, minimize redundant computation. Ensure total inference on test set completes well within 300s. Consider model size vs accuracy tradeoffs.
plan.success_criteria: Full pipeline runs within 200s on validation set (leaving margin for test)

plan.title: Try RT-DETR as alternative detector
plan.hypothesis: RT-DETR (transformer-based detector available in ultralytics) may handle dense shelf detection better than YOLOv8
plan.description: Train RT-DETR-l from ultralytics on the same data. Compare detection mAP against best YOLOv8 model. RT-DETR may handle overlapping objects better due to attention mechanism.
plan.success_criteria: RT-DETR detection_mAP competitive with or better than YOLOv8

plan.title: Confidence threshold and NMS optimization
plan.hypothesis: Careful tuning of confidence threshold and NMS IoU threshold can significantly impact mAP on dense shelf images
plan.description: Sweep confidence thresholds (0.01 to 0.5) and NMS IoU thresholds (0.3 to 0.7) on validation set. For dense shelves, lower NMS IoU may be needed to keep adjacent identical products. Plot mAP vs threshold curves.
plan.success_criteria: Find optimal thresholds that improve final_score by 1-3%

plan.title: Self-training / pseudo-labeling on test images
plan.hypothesis: Using high-confidence predictions on test images as pseudo-labels for additional training will improve both detection and classification
plan.description: Within the 300s inference budget: (1) Run initial model on test images, (2) Use high-confidence detections as pseudo-labels, (3) Fine-tune model briefly on pseudo-labeled data, (4) Re-run inference. This is test-time adaptation. May be too slow — evaluate feasibility first.
plan.success_criteria: Measurable improvement in final_score, within time budget

plan.title: Final ensemble and submission optimization
plan.hypothesis: Combining best detection model(s) with best classification approach and optimized thresholds will maximize final_score
plan.description: Assemble the best components: detection ensemble (if beneficial), best classification method, optimized thresholds. Ensure everything fits within 420MB weight limit and 300s time limit. Generate final submission. Verify submission format compliance.
plan.success_criteria: Highest final_score achieved, valid submission generated
